title: AMIP sea-ice forcing (CMIP6 to CMIP7) has NCEP input steps that add about 1 million km2 of Antarctic ice after 2009 and slow Arctic ice loss by 40%; this biases AMIP feedback by about -0.2 W m-2 K-1
abstract: Question: earlier campaign work found step artifacts in the SST part of the AMIP boundary conditions (PCMDI-AMIP 1.1.x, from NOAA OI SST v2) and their effect on feedback estimates. Does the sea-ice part (siconc) of the same forcing also have steps, and do they matter for AMIP radiation? Approach: we put AMIP 1.1.9 and 1.1.10 (CMIP7) siconc, OI v2, the NOAA/NSIDC CDR v6 and ERA5 sea ice on one 1-degree mask (13,402 cells poleward of 40 degrees, 1979-2022). A blind optimal-partitioning search with a null-calibrated penalty found steps in the monthly differences. Two surface-albedo kernels (CAM5, HadGEM3) gave the TOA shortwave effect, and 11 CMIP6 amip runs calibrated it. Results: AMIP siconc equals OI v2 ice and is the same from CMIP6 to CMIP7. AMIP minus CDR has Antarctic steps at 1996-12, 2006-08, 2009-06, 2012-06, 2016-11 and 2018-07; four fall within 1 month of documented NCEP input changes (about 0.2 expected at random), and the Arctic has steps at the same months. The two references agree after 1992 (CDR minus ERA5 Antarctic steps at most 0.016 million km2). Relative to 1997-2006, AMIP has +0.9 to +1.3 million km2 more Antarctic ice in 2009-2016 and 2018-2022 (October-January +1.2 to +1.7), mostly at or outside the CDR ice edge, with a pause from November 2016 to June 2018. The 1979-2022 Antarctic area trend is +0.18 million km2 per decade in AMIP against +0.03 to +0.05 in the references (October-December +0.27 against -0.05 to 0.00); the Arctic decline is 40-43% too slow (-0.23 against -0.38 to -0.40). In all 11 amip models the TOA shortwave poleward of 50S responds to the spurious ice, at 0.94-1.87 times the CAM5 emulation. With this calibration the artifact adds -0.08 to -0.09 W m-2 per decade to the 2001-2022 TOA trend and biases the regression feedback (TOA flux on global temperature) by -0.16 to -0.21 W m-2 K-1 for 1979-2014 and 1979-2022 (model range -0.13 to -0.25). Limitations: the causes of the 2016 and 2018 steps are undocumented; references differ before 1992; the radiative effect is a kernel emulation calibrated only for southern shortwave in 1979-2014, without longwave or turbulent fluxes; the feedback bias is a regression estimate, not a rerun of AMIP with corrected ice.
